title: Chilled Gazpacho with Tomato, Cucumber and Pepper
summary: A silky, ice-cold Spanish soup of ripe tomatoes, cucumber and red pepper, blended with olive oil until creamy and sharpened with cider vinegar. Topped with a crunchy dice of fresh vegetables, it is the most refreshing bowl you can make on a hot day.
equipment: blender (or stick blender and deep jug)
large jug or bowl with a lid

ingredients.item: ripe tomatoes, cored and cut into chunks
red pepper, seeded and cut into chunks
cucumber, peeled and cut into chunks
cider vinegar, plus more to taste
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Blend the vegetables
steps.text: Tip the tomatoes, red pepper, cucumber, onion and garlic into the blender, working in batches if your jug is small, and blend on high for at least 2 minutes, scraping down the sides once or twice. Keep going until there are no visible flecks of pepper or cucumber left. A long, hard blend breaks the vegetable cells open fully, releasing juice and flavour and giving a smoother final soup.

steps.title: Emulsify with oil
steps.text: With the motor still running, add the vinegar and salt, then trickle in the 6 tbsp olive oil in a slow, steady stream. Within a minute the soup lightens in colour and looks creamy, almost like a dressing. Adding the oil gradually lets the blades break it into tiny droplets suspended in the tomato juice, which is what gives gazpacho its velvety body.

steps.title: Strain for silkiness
steps.text: Set the sieve over the jug and push the soup through with the spatula or the back of a ladle, pressing hard on the pulp. Only a small mass of skins and seeds should be left behind; discard it. Straining removes the fibrous bits the blender cannot break down, so the soup feels smooth on the tongue.

steps.title: Chill thoroughly
steps.text: Cover the jug and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until the soup is very cold right through. This resting time is not just about temperature: the flavours of garlic, onion and vinegar mellow and blend together, and cold also makes the soup taste fresher and brighter.

steps.title: Adjust and serve
steps.text: Give the soup a good stir, as it may separate slightly, then taste and add more salt or vinegar if it needs lifting. If it feels too thick to sip, loosen it with some of the 100 ml cold water. Ladle into chilled bowls and finish each with the diced cucumber and pepper, a few drops of olive oil and a pinch of black pepper; chilling dulls seasoning, which is why tasting at this stage matters.

tips: Use the ripest, most fragrant tomatoes you can find; they provide almost all the flavour, so pale, hard ones give a thin, watery soup.
A common mistake is pouring the oil in all at once, which leaves it floating on top; add it slowly with the blender running for a creamy emulsion.
Chill the serving bowls in the fridge for 30 minutes so the soup stays icy at the table.
Always season again after chilling, because cold soups need a little more salt and acidity than you expect.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and stir well before serving, as it can separate. Do not freeze, as thawing ruins the creamy texture; serve straight from the fridge, very cold. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
